Brand guidelines v1.0

IdleSwitch is a CTC rail terminal that runs itself. The brand is lifted straight off the dispatcher's panel: the same colours the app paints with, the same 45° turnouts, the same rule that a set route is lit and an unset leg draws dim.

The trains keep running.

firetailfab.com/idleswitch · github.com/zebadrabbit/idleswitch

The mark

A turnout. Grey track comes in from the left; at the points the route is set up the diverging leg — green, lit — while the straight-through leg carries on dim. That is the whole app in one glyph: the operator has already set the route and the trains keep running.

Rules

  • The angle is 45°, the panel's crossover angle. Don't change it.
  • In lockups the main track sits on the baseline and the set leg rises to cap height.
  • The dim leg is part of the mark; one-colour versions keep it at 30–35 % opacity.
  • The tile is the Panel colour with a Panel-border hairline, radius 17.5 % — the app's own panels.
  • Minimum: glyph/mark 16 px, horizontal 110 px wide, stacked 72 px tall.

Lockups & colour variants

Five lockups × five variants, all as SVG (outlined, no fonts) and PNG in logo/. color is the default on dark; color-light on light; mono-* for single-ink and photo overlays; accent when everything on the surface is already blue.

Clear space

The cap height of the wordmark — the height of the “I” — on all four sides. Nothing inside it.

↕ cap height↔ cap

Colour

Every value is from src/style.css and render.js. Void and Panel dominate; Text for copy; Accent for the one thing you can act on; Green for status that is fine; Amber and Red only for status that isn't — never decoratively.

Panel#121a2eHUD, docks, logo tile
Panel border#243052hairlines
Text#cfd6ealabels, “Idle”
Dim#7d88a6secondary text
Accent#5aa9ffhuman route · “Switch” · actions
Route green#39d353operator route · the lit leg
Amber#f0b429slow orders, MANUAL
Red#ff4d4foccupied
Track#8a93abidle track · approach
Track dim#3a4463unset leg
Signal lamps, only ever as lamps:#ff3b30#ffcc00#34c759

Train-type colours (X yellow, P amber, Z purple, M blue, C grey, G orange, I cyan, L green) are data colours for the board, not brand colours.

In the app

The compact HUD lockup replaces the plaintext in the top-left. 18 px tall in the 32 px bar; under 1160 px the glyph alone stays instead of the name disappearing. app/hud-logo.patch + app/assets/, no new dependencies.

Imagery

Real renders of the app at night (?ff=1500–1700 on the default 4-minute day): headlights, EOT markers, signal halos, lit platforms. Bare panel (H), zoomed two or three wheel steps so the terminal fills the frame, lockup over a Void gradient. Every plate in this kit is a real seed — lantern and qgxriz — so anyone can reproduce it.

Voice

Plain, declarative, a little wry. Short sentences; the README is the reference. Say terminal, panel, operator, route, signal, switch. It's an idle sim and a screensaver — “game” only when comparing.

  • The trains keep running. — primary tagline
  • A rail terminal that runs itself.
  • Sit back and watch a CTC terminal run itself.
  • Take the panel when you like.

Keep it observational and warm — it's a pleasure to watch, not a note that the viewer is surplus.

Don't

Don't re-angle the leg45° or nothing; no curves, no 30°.
Don't drop the dim legIt is what makes it a switch and not a chevron.
Don't recolour the leg red or amberRed means occupied, amber means trouble. The brand state is “route set”.
Don't put the colour mark on a busy photoUse mono-light over imagery, or the tile.
Don't set the wordmark in another faceUse the outlined SVGs; never retype it.
Don't add glow to the logoGlow belongs to the panel at night, not the mark.
